challenge.better_approach: A `cairn_test` database that is dropped and recreated by the tester would make every scratch table disappear at once with no registry. Rejected: proofs of the bus and the librarian exercise ownership in the real registry, and the per-owner ticket makes 'which database' the owner's, not the tester's; a scratch registry keyed by pid works in any database. A daemon sweeping on a clock is the drift memory names (reaching-for-daemons-is-drift); the tester already runs before every seal and is the event.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That a pid is a lifetime: on one box, /proc/<pid> gone means the minter is gone. Pid reuse could make a dead scratch look alive; the nonce carries HHMMSSffff so a reused pid with an older stamp than the process's start time is still dead — the sweep compares stamp to /proc/<pid> start time when the pid exists. Second: that no proof relies on a leaked table from a prior run. Measured: every leaked pid is dead and nothing can be reading them; if a proof goes red after the sweep, that proof was leaning on a leak and is the finding.
challenge.prior_art: test_bus.py _cleanup (the hand-rolled teardown, 5 copies across proofs); test_chat_pane.py _drop_table; bus.py:287 create_owned_table(self._delivery_table) (the silent companion); store.drop_table (the primitive the sweep uses); the tester's seal path (where the sweep hangs); memory claude-oom-kills-the-box (the SIGKILL that makes finally blocks insufficient).
challenge.real_collision: aa4463bbd067 says the old `cairn` database stays read-only until 'the scratch-tables ticket drops it'. Distinction: this ticket sweeps the scratch OUT of `cairn` before the migration; the drop of the emptied old database moves into aa4463bbd067's own voyage (its constraint is amended in the same act, by CC under the delegated ordering). No Law collides: Law 5 (history under way) does not cover Postgres tables, and a dead proof's table establishes nothing about right-now.

value.what: A scratch table cannot outlive the process that minted it: every proof-minted table is born through one store door that records its pid, is dropped with its companions on exit, and is swept by the tester when its pid is dead; the 9,075 leaked ones are swept now.

value: Every proof hand-rolled its own teardown because the store had no word for 'mine until I exit'. Giving it the word is Law 4; the 9,075 tables are what the missing word cost.
